changes: p4 Tārānātha: role 'commissioner' replaced by 'beneficiary' (dative 'śarmaṇe' = written for him; no likhāpita/lekhayāmāsa); kept 'owner'; confidence medium
Removed unverified exact CE day (9 July 1837) from notes; year ŚS 1759 = 1837 CE confirmed
Notes: added the 'api' reading and the catalogue scribe error

notes: The chronogram is vila/bila (9), iṣu (5), muni (7), bhū (1). Read right to left it gives Śaka 1759, which is 1837 CE. The tithi is guha (= 6, for the six-faced Skanda) and the weekday is ravau (Sunday). The exact CE day was not checked. The catalogue names Tārānāthaśarmā as the scribe, but the colophon has 'harinṛsiṃho 'py alikhat śrī-tārānātha-śarmaṇe' (Harinṛsiṃha wrote it for Tārānātha Śarman), so Tārānātha appears in the dative. The 'api' is odd: it could be filler for the metre, or it could mean 'Harinṛsiṃha also wrote', which would imply another copyist. Tārānātha's role as owner or beneficiary is inferred from the dative; nothing in the colophon says he commissioned the copy. 'nepāladeśāntare' may mean 'in the foreign land of Nepal', which would suggest the scribe was not from Nepal; this is uncertain.
